seo.title: TablePro vs DBeaver: features and editions
seo.description: DBeaver runs on Windows, macOS and Linux on Java and JDBC. TablePro is a native client for Mac, iPhone and iPad. Compare databases, AI, MCP and prices.

header.title: TablePro vs DBeaver
header.lead: DBeaver Community is a free, open-source JDBC client. Its paid editions add NoSQL support and other tools. Compare those editions with TablePro’s supported databases and features.

tablepro: Free access to supported NoSQL engines, including MongoDB, Redis and Cassandra.
Native drivers, with no Java or JDBC requirement.
Free MCP and AI chat with your choice of provider.
competitor: JDBC engines beyond TablePro’s supported drivers.
Paid tools such as a visual query builder, editable ER diagrams and scheduled tasks.

glance.intro: DBeaver has a free Community edition and paid editions billed per user, so several rows say which edition a feature needs.

diagram.label: ER diagram
diagram.tablepro: A read-only ER diagram, exported as PNG or SQL, free

items.text: Community connects to any engine that has a JDBC driver, including engines TablePro has no driver for.
The paid editions add a visual query builder, ER diagram editing, scheduled tasks and Git sync for projects.
Every supported engine is free, including MongoDB, Redis, Cassandra and other non-relational databases. DBeaver offers NoSQL databases only in its paid editions.
TablePro is a Mac app written in Swift, with native database drivers. DBeaver is built on Java, and its download includes a Java runtime.

The <link>AI assistant and the MCP server</link> are free in the Mac app. You choose the AI provider, and the MCP server lets clients such as Claude Code or Cursor use your saved connections without seeing a password.
<link>Compare & Sync</link> compares the structure or the data of two databases and syncs the differences. It is part of Starter.
The separate <link>iPhone and iPad app</link> is free, with no in-app purchases.
TablePro requires a supported driver. There is no generic JDBC connection, so check the <link>supported databases</link> first.
The ER diagram is a read-only snapshot, and there is no visual query builder or task scheduler.

switching.intro: Import connections from a DBeaver workspace, from Community or a paid edition. DBeaver can stay closed, and its files are not changed.
steps: In TablePro, choose <ui>File > Import > Import from Other App…</ui>
Select DBeaver and turn on <ui>Include passwords</ui>. TablePro decrypts the passwords DBeaver saved, so there is nothing to approve in the Keychain.

Review the list, decide what happens to any duplicates, and click <ui>Import</ui>. Folders become groups, and SSH tunnel settings come across. A connection to a database TablePro does not support arrives unchecked.
Before you remove DBeaver, open a connection that had a password to check that it came across.
after: SQL scripts, query history and keyboard shortcuts stay in DBeaver.

faq.question: Does TablePro need Java?
faq.answer: No. TablePro is written in Swift and talks to databases through native drivers. Drivers for common databases come with the app, and the others download the first time you choose that database.

faq.question: How do speed and memory use compare with DBeaver?
faq.answer: There is no reproducible benchmark cited here, so this comparison makes no speed or memory claims. DBeaver bundles a Java runtime; TablePro does not require Java.

faq.question: What happens to DBeaver connections TablePro cannot open?
faq.answer: They appear in the import list, unchecked, with the reason beside them. Nothing is imported for them unless you check them.

notes.dbeaver-bundled-jdk: The download includes its own Java runtime
notes.dbeaver-databases: Community connects to any engine that has a JDBC driver, but not to NoSQL databases such as MongoDB, Redis or Cassandra. The paid editions add them.
notes.dbeaver-ai-community-providers: In {edition}, an AI chat with OpenAI or GitHub Copilot. The paid editions add more providers and explanations of queries and errors.
notes.dbeaver-mcp-server: A local MCP server in the Lite, Enterprise and Ultimate editions from version {version}, which was in early access when checked. Not in Community.
notes.dbeaver-git-sync: Git sync for projects, in {edition} and above
notes.dbeaver-erd-edit-paid: View only in Community. Editing is in the Enterprise, Ultimate and Team editions.
notes.dbeaver-query-builder-paid: In every paid edition, not in Community
notes.dbeaver-task-scheduler: In the Enterprise, Ultimate and Team editions
